chapter: Return in 1965, pay and Preservation Hall
title: Union status and pay for brass band jobs
summary: They discuss whether bands were union and what Casimir and Young Tuxedo were paid, five or ten dollars, with funeral rates.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You never heard a band at a wedding or anything like that, huh? No. No. I'm trying to think of any non-union brass bands that were around.
I didn't know any of them were unions then.
Yeah. It was my impression, and I think you told me one time when I asked you,

what John Casimir and the Young Tuxedo used to get for playing those bands and those jobs, a large parade or whatever. And I remember that at one point you said they got five bucks a piece and at least they got ten. But whether you were just stringing me along... Oh, no. ...or whether that was an authentic... Was that a reunion rate on it?
Yeah, but they had special rates for funerals, and they'd give you a funeral rate for a short parade.
And I don't know why there was such a great funeral.
